 WPMS No. 3210 of 2016  Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
There is no representation for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing Counsel for the State.

3. Mr. Shobhit Saharia, Advocate for respondent no. 2/THCD.
4.
Petitioner is presently residing in District Dehradun, however, he is permanent resident of village Khand, District Tehri Garhwal.
5. According to petitioner, his land situate in Tehri town near Old Bus Station was acquired for Tehri Dam Project, but compensation thereof has not been paid.

It is further his case that his land situate in his native village-Khand (rural area) was also acquired for Tehri Dam Project, however, benefit under the Rehabilitation Policy has not been given to him inasmuch as he has not been allotted agricultural land in lieu of his agricultural land acquired from village Khand.

6. A counter affidavit has been filed by Director, Rehabilitation, wherein, it is stated that as regards the agricultural land situate in village Khand, petitioner's father executed a sale-deed in favour of Irrigation Department and received entire sale consideration in cash.
Since, it was not a compulsory acquisition under Land Acquisition Act, therefore, he was not entitled to any benefit under Rehabilitation Policy.

7. Paragraph 3(E) and (F) of the said counter affidavit is extracted below:-
"E. That it is submitted that as far as the property situated in urban areas is concerned, the total entitlement of the father of the petitioner was 200 sq.m.,
however, on the application made by the petitioners and his brothers, purely on humanitarian ground was considered and each of the brothers has been given 150 sq.
meters plot and accordingly, the petitioner has also been awarded 150 sq. meter plot WPMS/3210/2016 on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51433039/
1 in the rehabilitation area.

Similarly the brother of the petitioner namely Rajendra Singh has also been allotted 150 sq. meter area in MC13, Ajabpurkalan, Dehradun,
who has surrendered the sale on 28-3- 2001 and obtained the benefit in lieu of such plot.
F.

That it is relevant to submit here that at the time of surrendering such plot, a declaration was also filed in the form of affidavit by the brother of the petitioner that no other benefit shall be sought by the brother of the petitioner.

However, in any case, both the brothers were jointly entitled to a plot of 200 sq. meter only, however,
the authorities involved in the project considering the humanitarian ground, has individually granted 150 sq. meter to each for the brother and, as such, presently no such benefit is liable to be given to the petitioner."

8. Thus, from the stand taken by the Director, Rehabilitation, it is apparent that both petitioner and his brother were allotted separate residential plots admeasuring 150 square meters each, although,
as per Rehabilitation Policy, only one residential plot was to be allotted.
It is further revealed that petitioner's brother surrendered the residential plot allotted to him and received monetary benefits in lieu of such surrender.
Petitioner has suppressed these facts in the writ petition and has tried to create an impression as if no benefit was given to him for the land acquired from Purana Motor Adda.

9. Learned State Counsel submits that petitioner earlier also filed Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1496 of 2007, which was dismissed, however, petitioner has not disclosed filing of the earlier writ petition.

10. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that after availing the benefits under Rehabilitation Policy, he is not entitled to any of the reliefs, as claimed in the writ petition.
11. Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
12. No order as to costs.

(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 10.04.2024 U.U.
